Subject: Dedicated pool roll-in: preferred regions, burst profile, and MPO checklist

Hi Sarah / Jordan —

Great to kick this off. Per our intake call last week, Asterion will be moving inference traffic for the triage model to a dedicated GPU pool. Before we lock sizes and timeline I want to align on three things so we can produce an MPO (multipool onboarding) checklist for Ops:

1) Preferred primary region and secondary/fallback region (latency to your users and data residency constraints).
2) Burst/autoscale profile — typical QPS and expected 1hr and 24hr peaks, plus tolerated latency SLOs.
3) Networking and compliance notes (VPC peering, IP allowlist, SOC2 evidence needs).

To make this concrete, could you please: a) share a short 7–10 day traffic sample (QPS by minute if available) and b) confirm any EU data residency restrictions that would prevent selecting eu-west as a fallback?

Attached: Asterion_MA_Platform_Requirements.xlsx (the intake we discussed). Once we have the traffic pattern Ben and Markus will propose a region + burst profile and I’ll slot the MPO checklist items and target turnup date.

Proposed timeline: intake/traffic by 6/23, design by 6/27, staging turnup week of 7/7. If Asterion needs earlier, flag it and we’ll look at burst-only options for initial weeks.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

—Monica

All —

Thanks for the data, Sarah. Quick read and a recommended path based on Asterion’s constraints:

- Primary region: us-west (closest to your users and data stores).
- Fallback region: eu-west for compute only. We will enforce KV/cache residency in us-east via routing so no logs or persisted cache leave the US (requires routing policy + explicit cache pin).
- Pool shape suggestion: 4x A100-equivalent instances to start (steady-state to handle 45 QPS headroom at p95 target of 220ms), with autoscale to add up to +3 extra nodes for short bursts (scales on 60s rolling window, cool-down 90s).
- Burst policy: soft-burst allowed for first 4 weeks (up to +50% capacity) to cover digest spikes; after stabilization we move to reserved baseline + measured autoscale.

Pricing/commit: We can accommodate a 3-month ramp with a monthly reserved baseline and burst billing for overage. I’ll send a draft amendment to the MSA after we lock final node counts.

Attachments: proposed_multipool-design.pdf (diagram and routing/routing-policy draft).

Action items:
- Markus: confirm network prerequisites (VPC peering, NAT/egress IP expectations) and what netops ticket needs to look like.
- Monica: capture these in the MPO checklist and propose target staging turnup (Sarah asked for earliest 7/10; Ben to confirm pricing cadence).

—Ben

Subject: RE: Dedicated pool roll-in: preferred regions, burst profile, and MPO checklist

Ben / team —

Technical notes from infra:
- GPU selection: A100 class recommended for the triage model; if cost pressure we can propose q4 quantized nodes (T4-like) but will need accuracy validation.
- KV/cache residency: we will set up a US-based cache origin (us-east) with routing rules that pin write affinity to US. eu-west compute nodes will be configured with read-only access to a replicated, ephemeral cache that never persists to object storage. This meets Sarah’s constraint but requires explicit config for cache TTL and replication policy.
- Networking: VPC peering needed; we require a single dedicated VPC with a /26 for the initial pool and documented allowlist of outbound IPs. NetOps ticket template: include CIDR, desired peering window (2–4 hours), and expected test plan.
- Autoscale behavior: we recommend target p95 <= 220ms. Scale-up triggers at 70% GPU utilization or sustained queue depth > 30 requests for 90s; scale-down after 5m cool-down. For short digest bursts we will allow a warmup pre-scale hook (API call from Asterion to pre-warm cache) — Priyom can add a light-weight pre-warm endpoint to your CI if desired.

Risks: KV replication across regions increases cost and complexity; we'll avoid cross-region persistence. Also need to validate that your internal cert (for peering) is in the expected format (PEM + chain).

I’ll draft the NetOps ticket template and share by Monday.

—Markus
Director, Serving Runtime
